content:
Analyzing the impact of motivation on student engagement in laboratory skill education is of paramount significance for learning and academic prosperity. Physical laboratories, treated as experiential learning landscapes in scientific studies, foster high-level conceptual understanding amongst students. Also, student attitudes towards these settings can considerably influence the outcomes of skill training.

In light of the COVID-19 pandemic and consequent lockdowns, computer-based virtual laboratories (VL) have emerged as potential conduits for skill development and experimentation. Yet, the adoption of VLs has been hindered considerably by limited awareness and familiarity amongst instructors and learners. This study aims to explore the prime motivating factors that dictate the efficacy of VLs in imparting laboratory skills and tasks to students.

Data for the study was accumulated using an intrinsic motivation inventory (IMI) scale, self-reported survey responses regarding extrinsic factors, and a scale ranking instructor perceptions of VL. Independent sample t-tests and automatic linear modeling (LINEAR) were employed for data analysis.

Our observations suggest that animated graphic aids in VLs bear more influence on students' intrinsic motivation in comparison to e-book resources. In addition, the role of instructors emerges as a critical factor that heightens student motivation to conduct laboratory experiments using VLs. Moreover, the findings imply that sustained engagement or repetition in VL experiments can have a positive impact on students' practical performance.
